I'm a data engineering student who likes taking messy, high-volume data and giving it a shape people can actually make decisions from.

Most of what I build starts the same way — a raw dataset, a question, and a pipeline that has to keep running long after I've stopped watching it. I trained at Digital Egypt Pioneers Initiative in 2025 and at the National Telecommunications Institute's Big Data track in 2026, building ETL pipelines, Airflow DAGs, and distributed data workflows alongside working data engineers. Outside of that I build my own end-to-end projects, from a batch-and-streaming airline analytics platform processing over 20 million flight records, to a wearable device that helps caregivers support people with intellectual disabilities.

I studied at Fayoum STEM School through high school, and I'm currently working toward a degree in Computer Science and Data Engineering at Beni Suef University — looking for a data engineering internship where I can keep building things that hold up under real data.

// 04 · Selected work

Projects I've shipped

A mix of personal engineering, academic research, and a project built for people who needed it most.

Personal Project

Skylens — Airline Big Data Analytics Platform

An end-to-end big data platform analyzing US Bureau of Transportation Statistics airline data through both a batch and a real-time streaming pipeline. Airflow orchestrates ingestion in Docker, Spark handles cleaning and aggregation, PostgreSQL stores the results, and Superset turns it into live dashboards covering delays, cancellations, routes, and airline performance across more than 20 million flights.

AirflowSparkKafkaDockerPostgreSQLSuperset
View on GitHub
Personal Project

IoT Sensor Data API System

A small end-to-end IoT pipeline: an ESP32 board reads live distance readings from an HC-SR04 ultrasonic sensor and pushes them through a FastAPI service into PostgreSQL. A lightweight dashboard queries the latest readings and charts them in real time — the same ingest-to-visualize shape as my bigger pipelines, just running on a single sensor instead of millions of rows.

ESP32FastAPIPostgreSQLREST API
Project files
Academic / STEM Project

Care Provider — Assistive Wearable

A wearable device built with a school team to support people with intellectual disabilities — monitoring vital signs, tracking location, and alerting caregivers if the wearer leaves a defined safe zone. Simple buttons let the wearer request food, water, the bathroom, or emergency help, aimed at improving safety and everyday independence.

ArduinoGPSBluetooth (nRF24L01)IoT
Project files
STEM Research · Group Project

Future Energy — Thermoelectric Waste Heat Recovery

A 5-person STEM project that recovers wasted heat from hot surfaces — like a cooking pot — and turns it back into usable electricity with a thermoelectric cooler module built on the Seebeck effect. I helped research the underlying thermodynamics, run the prototype tests, and measure voltage and current output across trials to evaluate how efficiently it converted temperature differences into power.

ThermodynamicsPrototypingData Collection
Project files
STEM Research · Group Project

Use Your Impure — Water Treatment Prototype

A water-treatment prototype built to clean polluted marble-factory wastewater for domestic use, through a three-phase process — chemical pretreatment, physical filtration, and final polishing. We measured dissolved compounds, treatment time, and energy use before and after treatment, and got meaningful improvement in water quality while keeping energy consumption low.

Environmental EngineeringFiltrationMeasurement & Analysis
Project files
Academic Project

Intelligent Tic-Tac-Toe AI Agents

A GUI-based 5x5 Tic-Tac-Toe engine with three AI agents built from scratch — rule-based, Minimax with alpha-beta pruning, and a learning agent — plus Human vs AI and AI vs AI modes to compare strategy and performance side by side.

PythonMinimaxAlpha-Beta PruningGame AI
View on GitHub
ISEF Research Project

Saving & Surviving Train

A redesign proposal for Egypt's railway infrastructure, tackling both cost and safety — replacing iron wheels and rails with airless rubber tires and paved steel-style track. The analysis projected a drop in cost per kilometer from roughly 21M EGP to 8.5M EGP, alongside fewer human-error accidents and a longer infrastructure lifespan.

Data AnalysisInfrastructure DesignCost Modeling
